title: transition
description: The loop's record of the issue changed: it moved to a new state, or its step, attempt or notes changed. Written by the loop on every record change, and again after a re-claim. It carries the whole record, so the loop rebuilds a lost record from the newest one; to_state is the issue's state for the factory tools. A retried write can repeat it: count one per (issue, life, seq).

life.description: Which life of the issue: one per pass through the factory, named by when its claim started (seconds, base 36).

seq.description: The record's sequence in this life: one more on every transition.

table_row.description: The row of the loop's transition table that fired, for example T9 or U1 (v2 SPEC 4.3); recovered when the loop rebuilt the record after losing the step's outcome, and then via is recovered too.

from_state.description: The state before; null for a life's first transition.

to_state.description: The state after: the issue's state from now on.

via.description: A short code for what moved it, for example approve, fix:review, free:load, unknown:timeout, triage:retry, unreject, reclaim (logged again after a re-claim) or dual-write (logged again when the new log lacked it). An open list: handle a code you do not know.

seq_at.description: When this transition happened. Time transitions by this, not by the envelope ts: a transition logged again after a re-claim keeps its seq_at.

state_since.description: When the issue entered to_state; earlier than seq_at when the state did not change.

resume_to.description: Loop state, for the record rebuild: when to_state is queued, the state a new claim leads to; when parked, the state unparking leads to; when waiting, the state the loop resumes to once every condition in wait holds; null otherwise.

branch.description: The life's branch, fixed for the life.

pr.description: The life's pull request; null until there is one.

head.description: The head commit a step last confirmed on origin; null before the first push.

approved_patch.description: Loop state, for the record rebuild: the patch id the reviewer approved; null until an approval.

brief_url.description: The URL of the design brief comment; null until the designer posts one.

step.description: The step this seq runs: the state's own step, or triage; null while waiting.

attempt.description: The attempt of that step, from 1.

cut.description: Loop state, for the record rebuild: true when this attempt already had its one free re-run.

triages.description: Loop state, for the record rebuild: triage calls so far in this life.

fixes.description: Loop state, for the record rebuild: entries to fixing so far in this life.

round.description: Entries to reviewing so far in this life: the review round.

question.description: parked: the question for the owner; null otherwise. For people; never parse it.

kind.description: The condition: issue-closed (the issue is closed), pr-merged (the pull request is merged) or tag-contains (a release tag contains the commit).

issue.description: issue-closed: the issue number; absent or null otherwise.

pr.description: pr-merged: the pull request number; absent or null otherwise.

sha.description: tag-contains: the commit; absent or null otherwise.

repo.description: issue-closed and tag-contains only: the repository (owner/name, lower-case) the condition is about; absent or null means the loop's own repo.

wait.description: waiting: the conditions the loop re-checks each pass; null otherwise

why.description: closed: why the life ended (done: its work had already merged); null otherwise.

notes.description: Loop state, for the record rebuild: owner, triage and decline notes for this seq's step, oldest first. For people and the step's agent; never parse them.

pr_closed_at.description: Loop state, for the record rebuild: GitHub's closedAt of the newest hand-closed pull request the loop has handled, exactly as GitHub gave it (the loop compares it as text, so it is never reformatted); null when none.

lives.description: This life's number among the issue's lives since the count last started; the issue is rejected at the configured maximum.
